author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty on both surfaces
summary: Either form of the veterinarian directory - the page and the machine-readable one - can be narrowed to a single specialty, matched on the whole name and without regard to letter case. Naming no specialty leaves both forms behaving as they do today.
acceptance_criteria: Both forms of the directory accept an optional specialty selector, named `specialty` on each, and behave exactly as today when it is absent.
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, the directory page for it lists only those veterinarians.
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, the machine-readable directory for it returns only those veterinarians.
A specialty named in different letter case from the stored one matches on both forms.
Only the beginning of a specialty's name does not match on either form; matching is on the whole name.
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields the ordinary directory response with no veterinarians in it, on both forms - not a refusal, a failure, or a not-found.
A specialty value that is empty or all spaces behaves as if none were named, the way an all-space owner search does.
Narrowing happens before the page is divided into pages, so the page count and the paging controls follow the narrowed list rather than the full one.
Every behavior above is covered by tests.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search - NG-9 still declines it; only a whole specialty name narrows the directory
Narrowing by any attribute other than specialty, and narrowing more than one specialty at once
A new page control for choosing the specialty - the directory is narrowed by the request, not by a new element on the page
Narrowing the owner, pet, or visit surfaces
Changing what the directory shows for a veterinarian, or the order specialties appear in
notes: NG-9 narrowed and recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-06-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. REQ-VET-003 (machine-readable directory as a supported surface) is newly minted and needs no code work - the surface already ships and is already covered by a test; the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is not reused. Stale downstream statement for the design stage to fix: docs/system-design.md records the machine-readable veterinarian route as serving no requirement and pending removal, which no longer holds. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the shape ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization records: controller talks to a declarative Spring Data repository, no service layer, everything in the vet feature package. The owner search is the working template for it - OwnerController.processFindForm takes an optional parameter, strips it, treats blank as broadest, and delegates to a paged derived query whose Page totals already reflect the narrowed set. Three deliberate divergences from that template: matching is whole-name equality rather than prefix; blank routes to today's unfiltered read rather than to an equality match on the empty string; and an empty result renders the ordinary directory with no veterinarians rather than the owner surface's rejectValue/notFound re-render. No new package, type, or pattern - two derived repository reads, one request parameter on each of two existing handlers, and the parameter carried through the page links. See docs/system-design.md sections Package Structure and Contracts.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived reads matching the whole Specialty name without regard to letter case - one returning Page<Vet> for the page surface, one returning Collection<Vet> for the machine-readable surface. Neither carries @Cacheable (ADR 2026-08-06-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-queries).
Both VetController handlers gain an optional specialty request parameter; absent or blank branches to today's unfiltered read, so the no-parameter path is byte-for-byte what it is now.
vetList.html page links currently hard-code /vets.html?page=N and would drop the narrowing on every page move; the specialty must ride along, which means putting it in the model.
The Vets wrapper is untouched - only the collection handed to it is narrowed, so the machine-readable document shape is unchanged.

patterns.description: optional search parameter: null means absent, otherwise strip; blank is the broadest read, not a match on the empty string
paged derived-query helper - the narrowing lives in the query, so Page.getTotalPages and getTotalElements already describe the narrowed list
declarative derived reads on a bare Repository interface; the new methods follow the naming convention and are derived, not @Query

risks.risk: Caching a read keyed by a caller-supplied string in the vets cache, which declares no eviction and no size bound, lets any caller mint unbounded permanent entries. The specialty is deliberately not validated against the stored list, so nothing bounds the key space.
risks.mitigation: The specialty-filtered repository methods carry no @Cacheable. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-06-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-queries.md, because the decision is an absent annotation and leaves no trace in the source.

risks.risk: Reaching case-insensitivity through column typing or collation would reproduce the PostgreSQL owner-search defect that docs/system-design.md Known Defects already records - the same request answering differently per database vendor.
risks.mitigation: Express it in the query. Spring Data's IgnoreCase keyword generates upper(...) = upper(...) in JPQL, which behaves identically on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. Do not touch any schema.sql or collation for this slice.

risks.risk: The existing page links use Thymeleaf's __${...}__ preprocessing form, which evaluates its content as an expression before the template is parsed. Routing a caller-supplied specialty through it is expression injection, and string-concatenating it into an href leaves it URL-unencoded.
risks.mitigation: Build the links with the link-expression parameter form - @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})} - which URL-encodes each value. Never place a caller-supplied value inside __...__.

risks.risk: Narrowing the page after it is fetched would leave the page count and page links describing the full directory, breaking the eighth acceptance criterion, and would silently drop veterinarians from later pages.
risks.mitigation: The narrowing is a predicate in the repository query; the controller never filters a returned list.

risks.risk: The implementer pattern-matching on OwnerController will carry over its empty-result handling, which rejects the field and re-renders the find form. The sixth acceptance criterion requires the opposite on both vet surfaces.
risks.mitigation: A specialty no veterinarian holds renders vets/vetList with an empty listVets and HTTP 200 - no rejectValue, no alternate view, no 404.

notes: Reconciled the stale statement the prd-entry flagged: the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement and is pending removal is removed from docs/system-design.md, and REQ-VET-003 is wired into the Implements column for both VetController and Vets. That second edit also resolves a pre-existing inconsistency - the Contracts preamble says an em-dash marks one of three kinds of contract, and Vets was a fourth. Added docs/adr/2026-08-06-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-queries.md and indexed it in docs/adr/README.md. No design-doc-autofix records in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Resolution basis: the covering code was read directly from source (VetController, VetRepository, Vet, OwnerController, vetList.html, VetControllerTests), not resolved through the IDE oracle - no IntelliJ MCP tools in this run. Coverage note, no action required: the case-insensitivity and whole-name acceptance criteria name both surfaces, and the prd-entry's test list exercises them through the page surface; both surfaces share one repository method, so the machine-readable side inherits the behavior rather than getting its own named test. Vocabulary: Veterinarian and Specialty are the prose terms per docs/ubiquitous-language.md; Vets in backticks is the serialization wrapper, never the people.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Both VetController handlers share a private selectedSpecialty(String) helper that normalizes null/blank the same way the owner search does, avoiding duplicated stripping logic
VetRepository's two new derived-query methods carry full Javadoc including the deliberate absence of @Cacheable, with the reasoning cross-referenced to the ADR rather than restated
Method and variable naming is descriptive and consistent with the existing file style (selectedSpecialty, findPaginated, findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase)
vetList.html threads the specialty parameter through every page-link URL via Thymeleaf @{} link expressions rather than string concatenation, consistent with the existing paging-link pattern
New tests (VetControllerTests, ClinicServiceTests) are additive only, use named constants instead of magic strings, and follow the file's existing structure and matcher style
./gradlew checkFormat and compileJava/compileTestJava pass clean on the change set

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the specialty filter is a Spring Data derived query (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) with no @Query, no string concatenation, and no native SQL anywhere in the change - the parameter is bound, so the caller-controlled value cannot alter query structure. Sweep of src/main/java for @Query/createQuery/createNativeQuery found only the pre-existing static PetTypeRepository query.

Cache-key poisoning mitigation verified independently by reading the full VetRepository: both new filtered reads carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no @Cacheable, while the two unfiltered findAll methods keep @Cacheable("vets"). A caller-supplied specialty therefore never mints an entry in the eviction-less, size-unbounded vets cache. Matches docs/adr/2026-08-06-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-queries.md.

Case-insensitivity comes from Spring Data's IgnoreCase keyword in the method name, not from a schema change, collation change, or hand-rolled SQL - no DDL or persistence config is touched by the diff.

Template injection / XSS: every new page link in vetList.html uses the link-expression parameter form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}. No __${...}__ preprocessing form is introduced (grep -F '__${' over src/main/resources/templates shows only pre-existing occurrences, all outside this change set, and none binding the new specialty). The parameter form URL-encodes the value and Thymeleaf attribute output escapes it, so a specialty such as "><script> is rendered inert; the value is never written into an element body or a raw th:utext.

Input handling: VetController.selectedSpecialty normalizes null/blank/all-space to null, so a blank selector falls back to the unfiltered read rather than matching the empty string; the value is otherwise passed only as a bound query parameter and a model attribute consumed by escaped link expressions. No file path, command, deserialization, or reflection sink is reached.

Data exposure: /vets and /vets.html return the same Vet projection as before, narrowed rather than widened. No new field, no new endpoint, no authorization boundary crossed - both routes were already public reads.
No secrets introduced: scan of the source and docs diff for password/secret/token/api-key/credential returned nothing.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties, and gradle/ are untouched by the change set, so no dependency or version is added or moved and no new CVE surface is introduced.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Acceptance criterion 6 ('A specialty no veterinarian holds yields the ordinary directory response...on both forms - not a refusal, a failure, or a not-found') is verified only on the page form (theVetListShouldBeEmptyWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty asserts status 200, empty listVets, no model errors). The machine-readable form has no equivalent assertion - theMachineReadableVetListShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty only exercises the non-empty case. Unlike the matching-semantics criteria (case-insensitivity, whole-name), which are legitimately covered once at the repository layer because both surfaces share one query method, this is controller-level response-shape behavior (HTTP 200 with an empty vetList, not a 404/error) and is not exercised for the JSON endpoint by any test in the diff.
findings.fix: Add a controller test (e.g. theMachineReadableVetListShouldReturnEmptyResultWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty) stubbing findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(SPECIALTY_NO_VET_HOLDS) to return an empty collection and asserting GET /vets?specialty=<that value> returns status 200 with an empty $.vetList array, mirroring the page-form empty-result test.

approved_aspects: The VetControllerTests/ClinicServiceTests split holds: VetControllerTests stubs the repository and correctly restricts itself to controller-owned behavior (which read is delegated to, model attributes, view name, page-link encoding, pagination totals); ClinicServiceTests uses a real @DataJpaTest/H2 repository to assert the actual matching semantics (case-insensitivity, whole-name-vs-partial, empty-result) against both the Page and Collection query overloads, which is the right place to prove the query rather than a stub's programmed response.

Case-insensitivity and whole-name-only matching (AC4, AC5) are each verified once against real seeded data for both the paged and unpaged repository methods, correctly treating them as shared query behavior rather than duplicating a stub-only assertion per surface.

Test data follows the three-tier naming convention throughout (RADIOLOGY, RADIOLOGY_IN_MIXED_CASE, RADIOLOGY_PREFIX, SPECIALTY_NO_VET_HOLDS, PAGE_SIZE) with no mystery literals in the new tests, and totalPages in theVetListShouldPaginateTheNarrowedList is a value a reader can verify by hand from narrowedTotal and PAGE_SIZE.
Pagination narrowing (AC8) is directly tested: totals come from the narrowed Page and the page-link href is asserted to carry the specialty parameter through Thymeleaf's URL-encoding parameter form.

Mocking stays within the brief's policy - MockitoBean is used only through WebMvcTest (the sanctioned HTTP-boundary mock), and the new ClinicServiceTests reach for the real repository/database instead of a stub.
./gradlew test passes for both files (VetControllerTests and ClinicServiceTests), consistent with the build-pass record.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the specialty selector reaches the data store only through Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, Collection and Page overloads). Parameters are bound, not concatenated; the change set adds no @Query, no createQuery/createNativeQuery, and no native SQL. Re-verified by grep across src/main/java, not by recall.

Cache poisoning mitigation holds: the two new caller-keyed reads carry no @Cacheable. The only @Cacheable sites in the tree remain VetRepository:45 and :55, both on the unfiltered findAll overloads, so an attacker cannot mint unbounded permanent entries in the eviction-less 'vets' cache by varying the request parameter. The rationale is recorded on the method Javadoc and in docs/adr/2026-08-06-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-queries.md.

Case-insensitivity is delivered by Spring Data's IgnoreCase keyword in the method name, not by a schema change or a database collation change. The change set touches no .sql, no build file, and no datasource configuration, so no cross-database matching divergence or DDL surface is introduced.

XSS mitigation holds: every page link in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html uses the @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})} parameter form. Thymeleaf URL-encodes link parameters and HTML-escapes the resulting attribute value; no __${...}__ preprocessing appears anywhere in this template, so the reflected selector cannot break out of the href. Swept the whole templates/ tree for __${...}__, th:utext, and th:inline: the remaining preprocessing sites (fragments/, owners/) are pre-existing, outside this change set, and interpolate framework- or entity-supplied values rather than this request parameter. VetControllerTests#theVetListShouldCarryTheSpecialtyOnThePageLinks pins the escaped rendering (page=2&specialty=radiology).

Reflection surface: VetController.selectedSpecialty normalizes null/blank to null and otherwise passes the value through unchanged. The value reaches the response only as the escaped link parameter above; the JSON route (/vets) does not echo the selector at all, and the new empty-result test asserts a bare empty vetList array with no selector echo and no error text.

Data exposure: filtering narrows the result set and cannot widen it. No new field is serialized on Vets/Vet, no exception or stack detail is surfaced on a non-matching specialty (the read returns an empty Page/Collection, rendered as an empty list), and no PII or credential-shaped value appears in the diff. Grepped the change set for token/password/secret/key-shaped literals: the only new constants are test specialty names (RADIOLOGY, SPECIALTY_NO_VET_HOLDS).

Supply chain: the change set contains no build.gradle, lockfile, or dependency-descriptor change (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only confirms), so no new artifact or version enters the graph this pass and the CVE surface is unchanged from the previously approved state.

Delta since the prior approval is one added test (VetControllerTests#theMachineReadableVetListShouldBeEmptyWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty) plus a docs/system-design.md Contracts-table edit. Production code is byte-identical to the reviewed state; the added test introduces no new trust boundary and asserts the safe empty-response shape.
